answer: Reciprocal-vouch graphs form a trellis, not a mesh: each identity needs an edge co-signed by a distinct sponsor already earning, graded shale while provisional and crystal once that sponsor stakes a 50-unit bond and 30 days' fees settle. Sponsors get two edges per quarter, and a sponsored key must clear 40 units of real work before its vouch counts at the seven-sponsor quorum. A fake ring stalls: members can only vouch for each other, so no edge graduates past provisional and each attempt burns its bond plus fees.
